instruction: Convert the blog pages currently open in Chrome to PDF format and save them to /home/user/Documents/WebPages directory.

metadata.explanation: Task requires converting blog pages to PDFs and saving to WebPages directory. Evaluator verifies at least 2 PDF files exist and each is at least 1KB in size (non-empty files).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator only verifies that 2+ PDFs exist in target directory, but cannot verify they are the correct blog pages
No content verification: Cannot distinguish between correct PDFs from the specified URLs vs any random PDFs
No filename verification: Does not check if PDF names are derived from blog page titles or URLs
Size threshold (1000 bytes) too low: Real blog page PDFs would be 50KB+, corrupted/incomplete PDFs could pass
Incomplete coverage: Only checks location and count, not task correctness
Logic will execute correctly at runtime but has significant semantic verification gap
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add filename pattern verification (e.g., check if filenames contain keywords from URLs like 'agent' or 'human-data-quality')
Increase min_size_bytes to realistic value like 10000 (10KB) or 50000 (50KB) for blog page PDFs
Consider adding metadata verification using pdfinfo/pdftotext to check if PDFs contain expected content keywords
Add URL/title verification by extracting PDF metadata (Creator, Title, Subject fields may contain URL)
Alternative: Use Chrome DevTools Protocol getter to verify Print-to-PDF actions were performed on the correct URLs
